newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan reiterates rules for China ship crossings.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan reiterates rules for China ship crossings.

text.p: Taiwanese officials said on Thursday that the island's ports were ready to receive ships sailing directly from rival China as long as they were owned by mainland, Taiwan or Hong Kong interests and fly a Hong Kong or third-country flag.
"If they meet these two principles and mainland authorities approve, they will be allowed into port," a transportation and communications ministry told Reuters by telephone.

The official, who asked not to be named, reiterated Taiwan's basic condition that cargoes originating in communist China could enter Taiwan's port at Kaohsiung, but would not be allowed to pass through Taiwan customs.

Facing intense pressure to ease the ban, Taipei has proposed creating an "offshore transshipment centre" at Kaohsiung, where incoming mainland cargoes could be processed in bonded zones outside Taiwan customs for onward international shipment.

Arch-rival China has issued rules in a sharply different spirit, saying that since Taiwan was part of China, cross-strait shipping was a domestic matter that initially should involve Chinese or Hong Kong-flagged vessels.

The official was speaking in response to local media reports on Thursday that China's southeastern port of Xiamen had invited several Taiwan shippers to an April 8 ceremony to celebrate the start of direct shipping links across the Taiwan strait.
Taiwan has approved applications by about a dozen Taiwan shippers to begin such crossings, and the applications have been passed to port officials on the mainland.

Taiwan has banned such links since 1949, when the island was separated from the newly communist mainland by a civil war, although indirect cross-strait trade and investment ties have flourished since a political thaw began in the late 1980s.

Beijing has made no public response to Taiwan's proposal, which strives to preserve the sovereignty of its exiled Republic of China government by not allowing ships flying communist China's flag to enter Taiwan ports.
On February 23, the Hong Kong container ship Lien Fung made what experts called the first quasi-direct crossing, passing through Hong Kong harbour en route to Kaohsiung from Xiamen.

That unprecedented passage and several since, widely seen as an incremental easing of Taiwan's ban, was possible under a pact reached in Hong Kong on January 22 by Taiwan and China shipping executives with tacit approval of both governments.
